newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's two crude ports closed a third day - ports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's two crude ports closed a third day - ports.

text.p: Two of Mexico's largest crude ports remained shut for a third day on Thursday as a cold front continued to bring winds of about 50 km per hour to the area, port officials said.

Pajaritos in Veracruz remained closed as of 0830 local/1430 GMT because of strong winds and waves, and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state was still closed, although wind speeds were slowing and the port could reopen at midday, port officials told Reuters.
The third and largest of Mexico's crude shipping ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open amid mild winds, captain Jorge Luis Rios Macbeth said.
Pajaritos and Dos Bocas originally closed at 1200 local/1800 GMT on Tuesday, along with six other Gulf of Mexico ports. Cayo Arcas ships 611,000 barrels per day (bpd) of
crude, Dos Bocas 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos 399,000 bpd, according to the latest figures from state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
